subject: NimbusHealth private offer: hybrid commit + channel passback proposal
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-19T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer structure question for hybrid reserved + metered plan

Hi Mina,

We reviewed the earlier pricing note and have two open items before our procurement team can proceed:

1) Channel margin/passback expectations for private offers when we route through our preferred reseller (CloudReseller). On AWS and Azure we anticipate a mixed billing flow (AWS Marketplace + direct Azure Po), and we need clarity on how Redwood allocates passback vs list-price uplift to the reseller.

2) SKU mapping across clouds — we have internal licensing that treats reserved capacity and metered token usage differently and we need a clear mapping so we can reconcile with our finance team.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Provide a single private-offer PDF that lists both AWS and Azure SKUs with passback percentages per SKU,
- Apply an early-adopter credit for the first 3 months if we hit the 60% commit threshold, and
- Route invoices to NimbusHealth but send a separate commission remittance to CloudReseller?

If you can share a short counter-proposal (numbers) and a draft PO we can circulate internally. We’re on a compressed timeline — hope to finalize within two weeks.

Thanks,
Claire
Procurement 
NimbusHealth

Claire — thanks for the clear ask. Happy to put a concise counter-proposal together. A few quick clarifying Qs to make sure the numbers align:

- Expected 12-month committed spend target (USD) or preferred node-hours baseline?
- Is CloudReseller acting as a reseller (invoice to them) or simply receiving a commission remittance?
- Do you want passback configured as a percentage off list price per SKU, or as a fixed percentage of Redwood net revenue?

I can draft a PO and a two-column SKU mapping (AWS / Azure) and propose a passback schedule. Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday (10/22) morning PT? If not, I’ll send a written counter-proposal.

Best,
Mina Haddad

Subject: Fwd: NimbusHealth private offer - channel margin + SKU mapping (internal)

Team — forwarding Claire's request. Need quick internal alignment so I can send a written counter-proposal by end of week. Key constraints from procurement: mix of AWS Marketplace (AWS PO path) and direct Azure private-offer (Redwood Private -> invoice to Nimbus). They want a single document and explicit passback per SKU.

My suggested starting point (numbers are flexible):
- Reserved capacity SKU (12-month commit): passback to reseller = 15% of list price (or 15% of gross SKU value)
- Metered usage SKU (on-demand tokens): passback = 10%
- Early-adopter front-loaded credit: 6% of first 3 months' invoiced amount if they reach 60% of committed spend in Q1
- Invoice routing: invoices to Nimbus; commission remittance to CloudReseller monthly with line-item reconciliation

Operational notes / questions for ops & pricing:
- Connor: can we support the hybrid invoice path (AWS listing + Azure direct) in one private-offer artifact? AWS marketplace requires a Private Offer per listing; we can mirror the same passback percent in the Azure PO but the backend routing differs.
- Vanessa: reseller uplift — do we want to protect gross margin by using a list-price uplift on reseller-eligible SKUs rather than a blunt passback? That would preserve Redwood net while giving reseller a visible margin.
- Markus: check whether early-adopter credit should be modeled as a promotional discount (applied to invoice) or as a rebate issued post-quarter. Tax/recognition differences matter for finance.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm whether passback should be percentage-of-list or percentage-of-net (I prefer percentage-of-list for simplicity).
2) I will prepare a two-page PO + SKU mapping with explicit passback rows and a simple commission remittance flow.
3) If you all agree, I will send the draft to Claire Thursday morning (10/22) and propose the call.

Thoughts?

Mina

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhou <procurement@nimbushealth.com>, CloudReseller Billing <billing@cloudreseller.io>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-22T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private offer structure question for hybrid reserved + metered plan -- Redwood counter-proposal

Claire / Nimbus team — thank you for the patience while we aligned internally. Attached is a concise counter-proposal and SKU mapping; summary below so your procurement & finance teams can review quickly.

High-level proposal (all USD):
- Term: 12 months, start on signing.
- Commit bucket: $1,200,000 ACV (example baseline — we can re-anchor if you provide your preferred baseline).
- Reserved SKU (12-month node-hour equivalent): passback to CloudReseller = 15% of list price
- Metered SKU (on-demand token usage): passback = 10% of list price
- Early-adopter credit: 6% of invoiced amount for months 1-3, paid as invoice credit if Nimbus hits >=60% of committed spend in first 90 days
- Invoice routing: Redwood invoices NimbusHealth directly. Commission remittance: Redwood issues monthly remittance to CloudReseller with line-item reconciliation CSV.

Operational notes and clarifications:
- AWS Marketplace: We will create matching private offers per AWS listing with the passback percentage reflected in the offer notes. Azure: we will provide a single Azure private offer PDF that mirrors the same SKU & passback lines. The two offers are operationally distinct but presented in a single PO document for your convenience.
- Passback basis: percentage-of-list price per SKU (simpler for AWS/Marketplace reporting); we will include gross and net columns in the SKU mapping.
- Credits vs rebates: Early-adopter credit structured as an invoice credit (applied to Redwood's invoice) to keep accounting straightforward. If Nimbus prefers a post-quarter rebate, we can change the language but it will lengthen reconciliation time.

Attached deliverables (attached to this email):
- Nimbus_Draft_Private_Offer_v2.pdf (private-offer PDF with per-SKU passback rows)
- sku_mapping.xlsx (two-column mapping: AWS SKU / Azure SKU / list price / passback %)
- pricing_workback.csv (line-level calculation used to derive reseller remittance)

Next steps:
1) Review the attachments and confirm the commit baseline (I used $1.2M as an example).
2) Confirm whether CloudReseller will accept commission remittance (monthly) or requires invoice-to-reseller (if invoice-to-reseller is required, we need to reroute the AWS flow and update tax fields).
3) If you approve, sign the attached PO and we’ll issue the AWS private offers and the Azure PO within 48 business hours.

If helpful, I can join a 30-min call with your procurement and CloudReseller Tuesday (10/27) morning PT to walk the document line-by-line.

Thanks and looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Phone: (415) 555-0132
